cards.explanation: The answer is fled. The text says it plainly: "All your rulers have fled together, captured without a bow." So the people in charge ran, and they ran as a group (Isaiah 22:3). I think that's the group project nobody wanted to be in charge of.

The answer is into captivity. The rulers were "…captured without a bow," and the fugitives "…were captured together, having fled to a distant place" (Isaiah 22:3). Think about that, friends. They fled, even to a distant place, and still ended up captured. So the running ended in captivity.

The answer is False. The prophet says, "Turn away from me, let me weep bitterly! Do not try to console me over the destruction of the daughter of my people" (Isaiah 22:4). He asks people to turn away and not console him. I think this is a heavy moment, so let it be heavy.

The answer is the Lord GOD of Hosts. Verse 5 says it straight: "…the Lord GOD of Hosts has set a day of tumult and trampling and confusion in the Valley of Vision…" (Isaiah 22:5). The day belongs to Him. That's why the prophet's weeping carries so much weight.

The answer is gates. Verse 7 says, "Your choicest valleys are full of chariots, and horsemen are posted at the gates" (Isaiah 22:7). So the best land is packed with chariots, and the gates have horsemen posted there. A gate is the front door of a city, and I'd say that door has company.

The answer is the weapons in the House of the Forest. Verse 8 says, "On that day you looked to the weapons in the House of the Forest" (Isaiah 22:8). When the defenses were uncovered, that's where their eyes went. Remember it, friends, because verse 11 comes back to where they did and didn't look.

The answer is to tear them down for the wall. Verse 10 says, "You counted the houses of Jerusalem and tore them down to strengthen the wall" (Isaiah 22:10). They tore houses down to strengthen the wall. Imagine counting your own street just to see how much of it you can pull down.

The answer is looking to the One who made it. Verse 11 says, "…you did not look to the One who made it, or consider Him who planned it long ago" (Isaiah 22:11). They built a reservoir for the ancient pool's waters, but they didn't look to Him. That's the part that was missing, so don't skip it, bakers.

The answer is weeping. Verse 12 says, "On that day the Lord GOD of Hosts called for weeping and wailing, for shaven heads and the wearing of sackcloth" (Isaiah 22:12). That's a call to grieve. It's a sober call, and the next verse shows what the people did with it.

The answer is True. Verse 13 says it: "…there is joy and gladness, butchering of cattle and slaughtering of sheep, eating of meat and drinking of wine…" Their words were, "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!" (Isaiah 22:13). Verse 12 had called for weeping, so the feast went the other way.

The answer is never. The LORD of Hosts says, "Until your dying day, this sin of yours will never be atoned for…" (Isaiah 22:14). That's a serious word, and it comes right after the feast. I'd just let it sit for a moment, friends.
